[AUTH-1] Middleware silently bypasses auth on error/config
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: The middleware returns NextResponse.next() when NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing and also catches any error and allows the request through, effectively skipping protection. This exact pattern (early return on missing env + top-level catch returning NextResponse.next()) will let protected routes succeed unauthenticated if Clerk is misconfigured or middleware throws.
Impact: Any misconfigured env or transient middleware error can fully bypass authentication for protected routes (e.g., /api/admin/*), causing an immediate trust-boundary failure at scale. 
Fix: Fail closed — return a 5xx or redirect to sign-in when Clerk is unavailable (or gate the behavior behind an explicit “dev mode” flag), and avoid swallowing errors that allow requests to pass.

File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L60)

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Middleware silently bypasses auth on error/config
File: src/middleware.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: The middleware returns NextResponse.next() when NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing and also catches any error and allows the request through, effectively skipping protection. This exact pattern (early return on missing env + top-level catch returning NextResponse.next()) will let protected routes succeed unauthenticated if Clerk is misconfigured or middleware throws.
Impact: Any misconfigured env or transient middleware error can fully bypass authentication for protected routes (e.g., /api/admin/*), causing an immediate trust-boundary failure at scale. 
Fix: Fail closed — return a 5xx or redirect to sign-in when Clerk is unavailable (or gate the behavior behind an explicit “dev mode” flag), and avoid swallowing errors that allow requests to pass.

[AUTH-2] Unindexed clerkId causes full-table scans on auth lookups
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L1-L60) and src/app/api/admin/check-admin/route.ts (L1-L60), src/app/api/admin/abandoned-carts/route.ts (L1-L60)
Evidence: Admin endpoints map Clerk userId -> local user via prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) but schema User.clerkId is a nullable String with no @unique or @@index. Lookups by clerkId therefore perform table scans as the user table grows.
Impact: Every admin auth check (and any route mapping Clerk IDs to local users) will scan the users table under load, causing DB CPU and latency spikes and likely outages as user count and request rate increase. 
Fix: Add a database index/unique constraint on clerkId (e.g., @@index([clerkId]) or make it unique if appropriate) and migrate; also update hot-path lookups to use findUnique when possible.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-3] Admin password endpoint does plaintext comparison and lacks rate limits
File: src/app/api/admin/verify-password/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: The endpoint loads admin.password and performs if (password !== admin.password) without hashing (bcrypt) or any login-rate limiting. 
Impact: This enables credential guessing/brute-force attempts against admin accounts and allows cheap synchronous verification calls to be abused under load. 
Fix: Store and compare salted hashes (bcrypt/argon2), add request-based rate limiting (IP and account), and introduce exponential backoff/lockouts for repeated failures.

[AUTH-4] Clerk webhook user sync lacks explicit idempotency guard
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: The webhook verifies Svix and then creates/updates users via findUnique->update or upsert by email, but there is no explicit idempotency key or retry-safe guard beyond relying on unique constraints. 
Impact: Concurrent webhook retries or race conditions can trigger unique-constraint failures or duplicate processing under heavy webhook volume, increasing error rates and DB load. 
Fix: Make the webhook handler idempotent using Svix event id de-duplication (store processed svix-id/event-id with TTL) or use upsert patterns that are safe for concurrent delivery and handle unique-constraint errors gracefully.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-5] Webhooks use proper signature verification libraries
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts and src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts
Evidence: Clerk webhook uses svix.Webhook.verify and Razorpay webhook verifies HMAC with RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
